identification.summary: Scarlet Mimic is a threat group named by Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 in January 2016 after a seven-month study of a multi-year espionage campaign against Uyghur and Tibetan activists and those interested in their causes [S1][S2]. Unit 42 also saw attacks against government organizations in Russia and India responsible for tracking activist and terrorist activity [S1][S2]. MITRE tracks the group as G0029 [S5].
identification.firstObserved: Unit 42 (January 2016) said the attacks began over four years earlier, i.e. roughly 2011 or before [S1]. Trend Micro first described the FakeM backdoor in 2013 [S2].
identification.notes: Unit 42 later tracks the cluster as Golfing Taurus (per imported record). Unit 42 found some IP overlap with Putter Panda (APT 2) but did not conclude the groups are the same [S1]. No Microsoft Typhoon/Storm name is mapped in this record. Do not merge with Earth Minotaur (Trend Micro, separate Tibetan/Uyghur Android actor) [S6].

attribution.sponsor: Not attributed to a government by the primary vendor. Unit 42 said it had no evidence directly linking the attacks to a government source, but that the activity supports an assessment that a group or groups with motivations similar to the stated position of the Chinese government is involved [S1][S2].
attribution.confidence: Low to moderate as a state-aligned assessment; Unit 42 explicitly declined direct government attribution [S1]. Press coverage of Citizen Lab's work described the group as believed to work on behalf of Chinese authorities, which is a secondary characterization [S4].
attribution.basis: Targeting pattern against minority-rights activists and Russian/Indian counter-terror-related agencies, consistent with PRC positions [S1]; partial IP overlap with Putter Panda, not concluded to be the same group [S1].

objectives: Information gathering on minority-rights activists (Uyghur and Tibetan) and their supporters, which Unit 42 assessed as the group's primary mission [S1].

sectors: Government organizations tracking activist and terrorist activity (Russia, India)
regions: Communities in and around northwest China and the diaspora
targeting.notes: Unit 42 did not know the precise target of each attack but most aligned to the minority-activist pattern [S1]. Citizen Lab reported that servers used as Scarlet Mimic C2 later hosted Google-credential phishing pages aimed at Tibetan activists and journalists [S3][S4].

capabilities.summary: Primary delivery is spear-phishing, plus a 2013 watering-hole attack [S2]. Main tool is the Windows backdoor FakeM, whose C2 traffic imitates Windows Messenger and Yahoo! Messenger traffic; Unit 42 documented later variants after Trend Micro exposed it in 2013, when the group abandoned infrastructure and retooled [S2]. Unit 42 also linked Mac OS X and Android Trojans through shared C2 and saw FakeM, Psylo and MobileOrder as evidence of expansion from PCs to mobile devices [S1][S2]. Citizen Lab described a 2015-16 shift to credential phishing on reused infrastructure [S3]. MITRE lists FakeM, CallMe and Psylo as associated software [S5].

campaigns.name: FakeM exposure and watering-hole attack
campaigns.summary: Trend Micro first described FakeM in 2013; Unit 42 reports the group ran a watering-hole attack that year and later dropped infrastructure and malware and retooled after exposure.

campaigns.name: Phishing against Tibetan users on Scarlet Mimic infrastructure
campaigns.summary: Citizen Lab confirmed phishing emails sent in November and December 2015 and found former Scarlet Mimic C2 servers hosting fake Google login pages, indicating a shift from malware attachments to credential phishing.

campaigns.name: Unit 42 public disclosure
campaigns.summary: Unit 42 published Scarlet Mimic after a seven-month investigation, describing Windows, Mac OS X and Android tooling and targets including Russian and Indian government bodies.

campaigns.name: Citizen Lab 'Shifting Tactics'
campaigns.summary: Citizen Lab tied Tibetan-targeted phishing to Scarlet Mimic infrastructure.

diamond.adversary: Unattributed group with interests aligned to PRC positions on minorities; no government link established by Unit 42 [S1].
diamond.capability: Spear-phishing, a 2013 watering hole, FakeM Windows backdoor and variants, Mac OS X and Android Trojans, later credential phishing [S2][S3].
diamond.infrastructure: Actor C2 servers; some IP overlap with Putter Panda; C2 servers later reused to host fake Google login pages [S1][S3].
diamond.victim: Uyghur and Tibetan activists and supporters; Russian and Indian government bodies tracking activists and terrorists [S1].
diamond.socioPolitical: Monitoring of minority movements that have strained relations with the PRC government [S1].
diamond.technology: Windows endpoints, Mac OS X, Android devices, and cloud email accounts such as Google accounts [S2][S3].

gaps: Unit 42 report full text (unit42.paloaltonetworks.com) could not be fetched in this session; technical details of Psylo, CallMe, MobileOrder, exploited vulnerabilities and indicators were not verified from the primary document.

Activity after 2016 attributable to Scarlet Mimic is not established in sources gathered. Later Check Point (2022) Android reporting on Uyghur surveillance and Trend Micro Earth Minotaur (2024) were not shown to be the same cluster [S6].
No government attribution exists; the Putter Panda (APT 2) overlap is unresolved [S1].
Exact start date (one aggregator claims 2009) is unverified.
Unit 42's current Golfing Taurus profile page was not opened.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Key terrain is activist and diaspora communication accounts, personal and mobile devices, and regional counter-terror agency networks in Russia and India [S1]. STEP 2: Defenders in these groups often lack enterprise security and use cloud mail, which the actor exploited through credential phishing [S3]. STEP 3: Template is spear-phish or watering hole, then FakeM-family backdoor on Windows, Mac or Android, with mimicked messenger C2 [S2]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued collection against minority-rights activists. MDCOA is use of the same toolset and infrastructure against government or military personnel tied to counter-terror or regional security topics. Candidate indicators: Messenger-mimicking C2 traffic, mobile apps themed for Uyghur or Tibetan topics, reused C2 hosting fake Google login pages [S2][S3]. Low direct relevance to US DoD networks in sources gathered.
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. Situational awareness: treat as low-priority regional espionage threat with limited public reporting after 2016 [S1]. Authorities and coordination: targeting is primarily civil society, so response would be partner-nation or civilian-agency led rather than DoD; share indicators through existing intelligence channels. Mission assurance: personnel using personal mobile devices and cloud mail on activist-related or regional topics are the exposed population [S2][S3].
